newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers say budget fate in Congress hands.
newsitem.headline: India rulers say budget fate in Congress hands.

text.p: India's budget for 1997/98 (April-March) could be passed on April 11 before a vital confidence vote but approval depends on the Congress party, a minister in the embattled coalition government said on Wednesday.

The market-friendly budget presented on February 28 was called into question on Sunday after the Congress party withdrew its crucial support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition.

On Tuesday, coalition leaders said they were exploring the possibility of trying to push the ground-breaking budget, which would slash corporate and personal tax rates, through parliament before the confidence vote set for April 11.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Srikanta Jena told Reuters that the speaker of the lower house, P.A. Sangma, faced pressure to ensure the budget was not held hostage to the political crisis.
"There are a lot of people asking the speaker to see that the budget is through," Jena said. "If all parties agree, they can do it on the 11th also. Now the responsibility is of the Congress party."
Asked if the government had begun meeting political parties to make sure the budget was passed, Jena said: "There is nothing so far. The whole thing is in the Congress camp."
Attempts to salvage the budget hit a snag on Tuesday when the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said a budgetary vote could not be considered before the confidence vote.
For the budget to be passed, the minority government would have to work out an agreement with either the Congress party or the BJP.
BJP vice president K.R. Malkani said a vote on the budget could not precede the confidence vote because spending proposals need first to be discussed by parliamentary panels.
Parliament had earlier been scheduled to take up the budget, proposed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on February 28, after reconvening on April 21.
